plain: Too eager to please or obey powerful people

webster.text: Promptly obedient or submissive to the will of another; compliant; yielding to the desires of others, properly to the will or command of a superior, but in actual use, it often signifies yielding to the will or desires of such as have no right to control.

more.text: Servilely or meanly condescending; compliant to excess; as an obsequious flatterer, minion or parasite.

example.quote: Thus, each of the principal branches of the federal government will owe its existence more or less to the favor of the State governments, and must consequently feel a dependence, which is much more likely to beget a disposition too obsequious than too overbearing towards them.
